chapter: The Dallas nightclub and Jesse Stone's band
title: Jesse Stone teaches Budd to write; "Idaho" and "W.P.A."
summary: Stone inspired Budd's writing; Budd describes Stone's hits and the Congressional investigation of "W.P.A.", and his later career.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Let me ask you about that. Who inspired you to write, Budd?

Jesse STone inspired me to write. And even my handwriting is something like his. He copied so beautiful it was like it came out of a machine, and I used to ask him about writing all the time, and "How do you do, how do you distribute -- " (inaudible). a ninth chord
Where did he go to school, Budd? You told --
He's from the University of Nebraska.
Oh, University of Nebraska.
Right.
And he got -- what are some of the great things that he wrote?

"Idaho." He wrote "W.P.A.", which he was called to Congress and interrogated because they wanted to know what he meant by when he says work while you're playing and play while you work, and all of that. And this number would have made him millions, it was so great, but at this time the W. P. A. were building the Grand Central Parkway then, and they were building all this, and he was writ -- and so they
* Works Progress Administration, a New Deal program of the 1930s.

wanted to know what did he mean, work while you play and play while you work, and all that, and they made -- they killed the tune. He had just had a Glenn Miller recording on it. It was on its way to making him a million dollars, and he had to go before the Congress of the United States and try to explain to show that he was not subversive.
I see.

And it was a great thing, he told me, they interrogated him for days and days and days. And they found out that he was not a Communist, and was not, and he just had an inspiration to write something, and --
And this Jesse Stone came to New York later and essentially made recordings of --
That's right.
And in Chicago he was in Chicago for a few years (inaudible).
That's right, he was in Chicago.
You and I worked with him in Chicago.
That is true. This is the same man.
Same Jesse STONE.
And he's still here going strong, this man. [in New York.]
Is that so?
He's still here, and he's living in New Jersey, and he's working at some of the places like Holiday [New York]

Inn, someplace, all over the New Jersey -- what I was saying, he's got him a -- he's a very talented man still. He looks like a man of about 50's, 60's, still today. Very intelligent. He's made a lot of money with ASCAP, and BMI, and he's just a great producer, this man.
